data.name: Mangat
data.gender_notes: Mangat is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit root 'man' (meaning 'to think') and 'gam' (meaning 'to go'), Mangat signifies one who has the power to go forward and think wisely. In Hindu mythology, Mangat is an epithet of the god Hanuman, symbolizing his strength, courage, and intelligence. The name Mangat carries the meaning “Powerful, Victorious” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mangat usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful, victorious and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Name of Hanuman, symbolizing strength and intelligence in spiritual pursuits.
data.etymology: Mangat belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Powerful, Victorious.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mangat total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Mangat is a Hindu name that holds a significant cultural influence, particularly in North India. It is a strong and unique name, with its roots deeply embedded in Sanskrit language and Hindu mythology. The name Mangat carries an auspicious connotation, as it is believed to bestow upon the bearer the qualities of wisdom, courage, and intelligence, often associated with the god Hanuman.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mangat holds deep spiritual significance, as it is considered an epithet of the revered Hindu god Hanuman. Hanuman is the embodiment of strength, courage, and intelligence, and is known for his unwavering devotion to Lord Rama. The name Mangat signifies one who thinks wisely and acts bravely, just like the god Hanuman. It is believed that bearing the name Mangat can bring blessings of wisdom, courage, and divine protection.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Mangat is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Mangal,' which means auspicious or fortunate. The 'At' suffix indicates that the divine auspiciousness is present within the individual, encouraging good fortune and prosperity.

historical_references.reference: Mangat Rai Chauhan was a Jat ruler of the Chauhan clan, who ruled the region of Sirsa in present-day Haryana, India during the late 12th and early 13th century.

Another Mangat, Mangat Rai, was a Rajput king of the Sisodia clan, who ruled the region of Mewar (present-day Rajasthan, India) during the late 15th century. He is known for his military victories against the Mughals and his role in preserving Rajput rule in the region.
